title: token-level-observability: add detailed token cost/latency metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Nina Patel
description: Motivation: operators and SREs need token-granular visibility to diagnose cost regressions and latency hotspots introduced by recent model rollouts. This PR introduces token-level metrics (emit/compute/kv-cache latency and token cost units), spans to link token events to request traces, Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerting rules. Summary of changes: - New metrics: redwood_tokens_emitted_total, redwood_token_emit_latency_ms_bucket, redwood_token_compute_ms_bucket, redwood_token_kv_cache_hit_count, redwood_token_cost_units_sum, redwood_token_cost_units_by_model. Metrics are instrumented with labels: model, route, region, customer_tier, quantization_profile (careful to cap cardinality). - Tracing: add token_emit and token_compute spans to the existing request trace (uses sampling at 5% by default; full traces when an alert triggers). Spans include token_index and kv_cache_hit boolean. - Dashboards: Grafana dashboards added under telemetry/dashboards/token_cost_latency.yaml with panels for per-model P50/P95/P99 token latency, token-cost-per-request distribution, token cache hit rate heatmap, and a new route-level cost breakdown view. - Alerts and tuning: new alerts for token-level regressions: token-latency-regression (P95 token_emit_latency_ms increase >25% vs baseline 7d), token-cost-spike (>3sigma over baseline 24h), and token-cache-degeneration (cache hit rate drop below 85% for 30m). Alerts include runbook links and automatic annotated regressions in the console. - Runtime safeguards: added cardinality caps and label whitelists to avoid high-cardinality explosions (configurable via telemetry.config.token_labels). - Tests/QA: unit tests for metric label sanitization and end-to-end integration test that validates metrics emitted for synthetic request traces. CI: lint, unit, and integration jobs added; flaky integration test fixed by increasing wait time for KV cache warmup. Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive and will not break existing dashboards. Checklist: - [x] Add token-level metrics and labels - [x] Add tracing spans and sampling policy - [x] Add Grafana dashboard YAML and example panels - [x] Add alerts and runbook references - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Add docs section in observability docs (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/observability/token-metrics) Implementation notes: metric names follow the existing redwood_* prefix and Prometheus exposition conventions. Bucket boundaries chosen after sampling production traffic (1ms, 2ms, 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, +inf) to capture token-level latency distribution. To reduce cardinality, we truncate model and route names and only allow a configurable set of quantization_profile values. Traces link back to request IDs and include sampled token sequences for debugging. Operational notes: dashboards are staged in the Grafana provisioning directory; alerts were tuned to minimize noise during release ramp by using relative regression thresholds and excluding low-volume routes. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/token-observability. Related: ENG-789 (token observability epic), PM-214 (product request for per-token billing visibility).
commits: Add token metrics and label sanitization (instrumentation/metrics_collector.py)
Add token spans and sampling policy (runtime/tracing/span_instrumentation.py)
Add Grafana dashboards and alert rules (telemetry/dashboards/token_cost_latency.yaml)
Tests: unit + integration for token metrics and traces (telemetry/tests/test_token_metrics.py)
review_comments: Omar Reyes: Please add a cardinality note in the metrics docs and ensure quantization_profile is whitelisted. Reply (Nina): added note + config flag telemetry.config.token_labels. PTAL.

Leah Chen: The P95 regression alert looks noisy on low-volume routes. Suggest adding a minimum-volume filter. Reply (Nina): implemented min_request_volume=100 in alert rule and added annotation to dashboard.

Mateo Alvarez: Can we avoid emitting token spans for high-throughput inference paths? Suggest sampling or conditional spans. Reply (Nina): implemented 5% default sampling with conditional full dumps on alert and added config runtime.tracing.token_span_sampling.
CI bot: integration tests failed on first run due to KV cache warmup race. Retry triggered and CI passed on second run.
release_notes: Add token-level cost and latency metrics, dashboards, and tuned alerts. Operators can now diagnose token-level regressions and attribute cost to model/route. Includes cardinality controls and runbook.
notes: Deployed to staging for 24h smoke tests. No significant noise observed after tuning. Will monitor for first 72h post-merge and iterate on alert thresholds.
